cards.front: Who narrates Ḥadīth 1 of the Arbaʿīn?
cards.back: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb RA

cards.meaning: commander of the believers — ʿUmar RA was the first given this title

cards.front: From which tribe and sub-tribe was ʿUmar RA?
cards.back: Quraysh, of the sub-tribe al-ʿAdawī

cards.front: Which of the four rightly-guided khalīfahs was ʿUmar RA?
cards.back: The second

cards.front: What was ʿUmar RA known for in the time of Jāhiliyyah?
cards.back: A high position, and his strength, courage, bravery, and intelligence

cards.front: In which year of prophethood did ʿUmar RA accept Islam?
cards.back: The sixth

cards.front: How many Muslims were there when ʿUmar RA accepted Islam?
cards.back: Forty men and eleven women

cards.front: What did Ibn Masʿūd RA say changed with ʿUmar's RA acceptance of Islam?
cards.back: The Muslims could not pray at the Kaʿbah until he accepted

cards.front: What was distinctive about ʿUmar's RA migration?
cards.back: He migrated openly, in defiance of the Quraysh, rather than secretly

cards.front: In how many of the Prophet's ﷺ battles did ʿUmar RA participate?
cards.back: All of them

cards.front: When was ʿUmar RA selected as khalīfah?
cards.back: The day Abū Bakr RA passed away

cards.front: How far did the borders of Islam expand under ʿUmar RA?
cards.back: East to the borders of China, and west to North Africa

cards.front: Which lands did ʿUmar RA open?
cards.back: Shām, Iraq, al-Quds, and Egypt

cards.front: How many masājid are said to have been established during ʿUmar's RA khilāfah?
In what year was ʿUmar RA martyred?
cards.back: The year 23

cards.front: Who killed ʿUmar RA, and during what?
cards.back: Abū Luʾluʾ al-Majūsī, while he was praying Fajr

cards.front: How long did ʿUmar RA live after being stabbed?
cards.back: Three days

cards.front: How is the ḥadīth on intentions (Arbaʿīn 1) described in terms of its place in Islam?
cards.back: It is the axis around which Islam revolves

cards.front: In the discussion of the ḥadīth on intentions, what must accompany islām — external submission — for its acts to be accepted?
cards.back: Sincerity

cards.front: What did Imām Abū Dāwūd say about the ḥadīth on intentions?
cards.back: That it is half of Islam

cards.front: What did Imām al-Shāfiʿī say the ḥadīth on intentions encompasses?
cards.back: Half of knowledge

cards.front: Why is the ḥadīth on intentions said to be half of knowledge?
cards.back: A person's actions and knowledge divide into internal and external, and the ḥadīth on intentions deals with the internal

cards.front: On what reasoning did Imām al-Shāfiʿī and Imām Aḥmad call the ḥadīth on intentions one-third of knowledge?
cards.back: Actions come from three places — the heart, the tongue, and the limbs — and sincerity is found in the heart

cards.text: On the ḥadīth on intentions, Imām al-Shāfiʿī is reported both ways: {{c1::half}} of knowledge, on the internal/external division; and {{c2::one-third}} of knowledge, on the heart/tongue/limbs division
cards.extra: Two different partitions of knowledge, hence two different fractions.

cards.front: What is famously absent from Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, and what stands in its place?
cards.back: It has no muqaddimah — al-Bukhārī opens with the ḥadīth on intentions instead, as a reminder to himself and the reader

cards.front: Who was مُهَاجِر أُمّ قَيْس, and how did he get the name?
cards.back: A Companion who proposed to a woman called Umm Qays in Madinah; she refused unless he migrated, so he migrated in order to marry her

cards.front: What does إِنَّمَا do to the connection between مُبْتَدَأ and خَبَر?
cards.back: It makes it exclusive

cards.front: What effect does <bdi>إِنَّمَا</bdi> have on the grammatical state of the word after it?
cards.back: None — it is <bdi>غَيْر عَامِل</bdi>

cards.front: In the ḥadīth on intentions, what does <bdi>عَمَل</bdi> (action) cover?
cards.back: Any action we do voluntarily

cards.front: What is نِيَّة, technically?
cards.back: The determination, want, and aspiration to do something

cards.front: How did Ibn al-Qayyim define نِيَّة?
cards.back: The knowledge of the doer of what he is doing, and the purpose behind the action

cards.front: What happens if the intention behind a deed is not sincere?
cards.back: The reward is not received — and the person may even be liable

cards.front: What does “every person will only get what they intended” imply when one deed carries several good intentions?
cards.back: A reward for each of them

cards.front: What follows practically from being rewarded for multiple intentions?
cards.back: We should be very intentional in what we do, to gain as much reward as possible

cards.front: What can a sincere intention do to an everyday act?
cards.back: Transform it into an act of worship

cards.front: If the purpose of our existence is to worship Allah, what does that actually require?
cards.back: Not being in ṣalāh constantly, but living in accordance with divine guidance — the whole of life becomes ʿibādah through intention

cards.front: Which act is used as the example in the ḥadīth on intentions?
cards.back: Hijrah

cards.front: Why was hijrah such a demanding act of worship when it was required?
cards.back: It was under threat of persecution, and meant abandoning one's wealth and family

cards.front: Which acts demand the most care with intention?
cards.back: Anything public-facing

cards.text: Guarding the intention, per the ḥadīth on intentions — before an act: {{c1::take a moment to be intentional}}; during it: {{c2::remind yourself of the intention}}; after it: {{c3::seek istighfār for any deficiency}}

cards.front: What does إِخْلَاص mean?
cards.back: To dedicate, to be loyal, devoted, or faithful

cards.front: What meaning do the root letters of إِخْلَاص convey?
cards.back: Purifying or cleaning something

cards.front: What is إِخْلَاص, as an act?
cards.back: To worship Allah with the sole objective of attaining His nearness

cards.front: What is a good proxy for testing your own sincerity?
cards.back: Ask: who do I want the reward from — Allah, or the people?

cards.front: What role does sincerity play in whether a deed is accepted?
cards.back: It is a precondition for the acceptance of anything we do

cards.front: When is there reward for an intention that was never acted on?
cards.back: When a valid excuse prevented the action

cards.front: What is the “new” hijrah?
cards.back: Abandoning sins and mistakes

cards.front: What three harms come from love of this world?
cards.back: It is a disruptive disease of the heart; it corrupts acts of worship; it distracts from the hereafter and the purpose of our existence

cards.front: What did the Prophet ﷺ not do when correcting someone?
cards.back: Call them out in public, embarrass them, or scold them

cards.front: How does the ḥadīth on intentions itself illustrate the prophetic method of correction?
cards.back: He did not single out the individual — he turned it into a teaching moment and used it to explain a general principle

cards.text: بُنِيَ الإِسْلَامُ عَلَى خَمْسٍ: {{c1::شَهَادَةِ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللهِ}}، وَ{{c2::إِقَامِ الصَّلَاةِ}}، وَ{{c3::إِيتَاءِ الزَّكَاةِ}}، وَ{{c4::حَجِّ البَيْتِ}}، وَ{{c5::صَوْمِ رَمَضَانَ}}
cards.extra: Ḥadīth 3 of the Arbaʿīn, narrated by Ibn ʿUmar. Check the wording against your copy — supplied, not taken from your notes.

cards.text: {{c1::بُنِيَ الإِسْلَامُ}} عَلَى {{c2::خَمْسٍ}}

cards.front: How does the ḥadīth of the five pillars open, and what image does it use?
cards.back: <bdi>بُنِيَ الإِسْلَامُ عَلَى خَمْسٍ</bdi> — “Islam is built upon five” — the image of a building

cards.front: Who narrates the ḥadīth of the five pillars?
cards.back: Ibn ʿUmar — son of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb

cards.front: When was Ibn ʿUmar born?
cards.back: Two years after the message began

cards.front: When and how did Ibn ʿUmar accept Islam?
cards.back: As a child alongside his father, before reaching puberty

cards.front: At what age did Ibn ʿUmar migrate?
cards.back: Eleven, with his parents

cards.front: Why was Ibn ʿUmar turned away from Badr and Uḥud?
cards.back: He was not yet fifteen

cards.front: Which was Ibn ʿUmar's first battle?
cards.back: Khandaq

cards.front: What standing did Ibn ʿUmar have among the Companions?
cards.back: One of the most knowledgeable, and one of those who would give fatwa

cards.front: How many aḥādīth did Ibn ʿUmar narrate?
In what year did Ibn ʿUmar die?
How far did Ibn ʿUmar take following the sunnah?
cards.back: He followed every sunnah, even the <bdi>سُنَن الزَّوَائِد</bdi>

cards.front: What story is told of Ibn ʿUmar ducking while travelling?
cards.back: There had once been a tree there and the Prophet ﷺ had ducked, so he ducked too

cards.front: Which ḥadīth is the origin of the five pillars of Islam?
cards.back: Ḥadīth 3 of the Arbaʿīn, narrated by Ibn ʿUmar — <bdi>بُنِيَ الإِسْلَامُ عَلَى خَمْسٍ</bdi>

cards.front: What do the five pillars represent in relation to Allah?
cards.back: Our external submission to Him

cards.front: What comparison does the Prophet ﷺ draw in the ḥadīth of the five pillars?
cards.back: Islam to a strong building raised on a firm foundation, without which it would be useless

cards.front: In the building image of the ḥadīth of the five pillars, which pillar is central, and where do the others stand?
cards.back: The shahādah is the central pillar; the other four stand at the corners

cards.front: Why does the ḥadīth of the five pillars not make obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions optional?
cards.back: A building is not complete without walls, doors and furniture — and those are the commands and prohibitions

cards.front: What does the shahādah do that no other pillar does?
cards.back: It enters a person into the fold of Islam

cards.front: What is the shahādah, in terms of heart and tongue?
cards.back: A verbal expression of the faith that lies in the heart

cards.front: What three things does saying the shahādah affirm?
cards.back: The existence and oneness of Allah, the nubuwwah of the Prophet ﷺ, and all of his teachings

cards.front: Testimony in a court rests on first-hand experience — what does that imply for the shahādah?
cards.back: That it is said on the basis of one's own experience, understanding and knowledge

cards.front: What did the Prophet ﷺ promise for saying the shahādah sincerely?
cards.back: Whoever says it with sincerity and true belief will enter paradise

cards.front: What does accepting Islam do to what came before it?
cards.back: It wipes away whatever the person did before entering Islam

cards.meaning: the great pillar of the religion — a name for the ṣalāh
the finest of the acts of obedience — a name for the ṣalāh

cards.front: What does a sincere, mindful, correct prayer engage?
cards.back: The entire being, comprehensively

cards.front: Which verb does Allah use for prayer instead of “pray”, and why does it matter?
cards.back: <bdi>أَقَامَ</bdi> — to establish. It means to make something straight and upright without deficiency

cards.text: <bdi>إِقَامَة الصَّلَاة</bdi> externally is {{c1::praying properly, at its time, with its preconditions, integrals and sunan}}; internally it is {{c2::praying with purpose, meaning, understanding and humility}}
{{c1::<bdi>خُشُوع</bdi>}} is humility; {{c2::<bdi>خُضُوع</bdi>}} is being in a state of need

cards.front: How did Ibn ʿAbbās describe establishing the prayer?
cards.back: Performing its bowing, prostrations and recitation completely, with fear of Allah and complete attention

cards.front: Complete the ḥadīth about the Prophet's ﷺ love of prayer: “The coolness of …”
cards.back: …my eyes was placed in prayer — an Arabic expression for happiness, tranquility and contentment

cards.front: What is unique about how the command to pray was given?
cards.back: Jibrīl took the Prophet ﷺ up into the heavens to receive it, rather than bringing it down

cards.front: What is the first thing a person is asked about on the Day of Judgement?
cards.back: The prayer

cards.front: What do a minority of scholars hold about deliberately leaving the prayer?
cards.back: That the person has left Islam

cards.front: Complete the ḥadīth: “Between a man and disbelief is …”
cards.back: …leaving the prayer

cards.front: Complete the ḥadīth: “The treaty I have with my followers is the prayer — …”
cards.back: …whoever leaves it, it is as if he has disbelieved

cards.front: What was among the last things the Prophet ﷺ said as he was leaving this world?
cards.back: “Your prayer, your prayer, and those in your care”

cards.front: What does the majority hold about the aḥādīth that call leaving the prayer disbelief?
cards.back: That they show how heavily the prayer is emphasised — not that the person leaves Islam

cards.front: What does the Qurʾān say prayer prevents?
cards.back: Obscenities and evil — what the Sharīʿah dislikes and prohibits

cards.front: If someone prays regularly yet still commits obscenities and evil, what follows?
cards.back: The prayer itself needs fixing

cards.front: How should the day be arranged around the prayer?
cards.back: Ṣalāh should be the priority with everything else revolving around it, rather than being fitted in

cards.meaning: the sweetness of faith — when ṣalāh is enjoyable rather than a burden

cards.front: What did Ibn Qudāmah say about a heart not present in prayer?
cards.back: That its cause is weakness of īmān — so strive and struggle to strengthen it

cards.front: Which two pillars are most commonly mentioned together in the Qurʾān and Sunnah?
cards.back: Ṣalāh and zakāh

cards.front: What does zakāh purify, and what does it purify the heart from?
cards.back: It purifies and increases wealth, and purifies the heart of greed, stinginess and love of wealth and possessions

cards.front: What makes ḥajj distinctive among the pillars in what it demands?
cards.back: It involves both the body and wealth

cards.front: What opportunity does ḥajj present?
cards.back: To completely change one's life and start over

cards.front: What did the Prophet ﷺ promise one who performs ḥajj without obscenity or sin?
cards.back: He returns like the day his mother gave birth to him — sinless

cards.front: What did the Prophet ﷺ say the reward of an accepted ḥajj is?
cards.back: Nothing other than Jannah

cards.front: Complete the ḥadīth qudsī on fasting: “Every act of the son of Adam is for himself except fasting — …”
cards.back: …for it is for Me, and I give the reward for it

cards.text: The ḥadīth “every act of the son of Adam is for himself except fasting” shows two things: {{c1::how sincere the act is, since it has no outward aspect}}, and {{c2::that its reward cannot be transferred, unlike other good deeds which can be taken in recompense for wronging someone}}

cards.front: What does the Qurʾān say fasting develops?
cards.back: Taqwā

cards.front: What did the Prophet ﷺ promise one who fasts Ramaḍān with īmān and hope of reward?
cards.back: All of his previous sins are forgiven

cards.front: Where do the voluntary acts belong relative to the five pillars?
cards.back: After the foundations are established

cards.front: What other narration of the five pillars exists, and who narrates it?
cards.back: One placing Ramaḍān before ḥajj — both narrated by Ibn ʿUmar

cards.front: How did Ibn ʿUmar answer the student who objected when he narrated the five pillars with Ramaḍān before ḥajj?
cards.back: That he had heard both orders from the Prophet ﷺ

cards.front: What are the five acts of worship not meant to be, and what are they meant to be?
cards.back: Not rituals — they have higher objectives and aims, and are meant to be transformative, changing a person's life and strengthening their relationship with Allah

cards.front: Which ḥadīth of the Arbaʿīn is called <bdi>أُمّ الحَدِيث</bdi>?
cards.back: Ḥadīth 2 — Ḥadīth Jibrīl

cards.front: <bdi>أُمّ الحَدِيث</bdi> is named on the model of which other title?
cards.back: <bdi>أُمّ القُرْآن</bdi> — al-Fātiḥah

cards.front: According to Ibn Ḥajar, when in the Prophet's ﷺ life did the event of Ḥadīth Jibrīl take place?
cards.back: Near the end of his life

cards.text: In Ḥadīth Jibrīl, the man seemed a traveller because {{c1::no one present knew him}}, yet {{c2::his clothes were clean and he bore no marks of travel}}

In Ḥadīth Jibrīl the four questions are about {{c1::<bdi>الإِسْلَام</bdi> (Islām)}}, {{c2::<bdi>الإِيمَان</bdi> (Īmān)}}, {{c3::<bdi>الإِحْسَان</bdi> (Iḥsān)}}, and {{c4::<bdi>السَّاعَة</bdi> (the Hour)}}
cards.extra: In the order they are asked.

cards.front: In Ḥadīth Jibrīl, how does the Prophet ﷺ answer “What is Islām?”
cards.back: With the five pillars

cards.text: <bdi>إِسْلَام</bdi>, <bdi>إِيمَان</bdi> and <bdi>إِحْسَان</bdi> are the <bdi>مَصَادِر</bdi> of {{c1::<bdi>أَسْلَمَ</bdi>}}, {{c2::<bdi>آمَنَ</bdi>}} and {{c3::<bdi>أَحْسَنَ</bdi>}} — all Form {{c4::IV}}

cards.front: What does <bdi>إِسْلَام</bdi> mean linguistically?
cards.back: Obedience, servitude

cards.text: Technically, <bdi>الإِسْلَام</bdi> has two definitions: {{c1::the proper name of the entire way of life revealed by Allah}}, and {{c2::external submission — <bdi>الاِنْقِيَادُ الظَّاهِرِيُّ</bdi>}}

cards.front: Why did the Prophet ﷺ define Islām by the five pillars?
cards.back: Because Islām, technically, is external submission — <bdi>الاِنْقِيَادُ الظَّاهِرِيُّ</bdi>

cards.front: In defining Islām by five pillars, what did the Prophet ﷺ intend the five to stand for?
cards.back: Five categories of submission — not a limit on what Islām is

cards.text: The five pillars as categories of submission: shahādah — {{c1::verbal}}; prayer — {{c2::physical}}; fasting — {{c3::refraining}}; zakāh — {{c4::financial}}; ḥajj — {{c5::all of them together}}

cards.front: In Ḥadīth Jibrīl, the Prophet's ﷺ answer about īmān is not a definition — what does it do instead?
cards.back: It describes what one must believe in — the six pillars of faith

cards.text: The six pillars of faith in Ḥadīth Jibrīl: belief in {{c1::Allah}}, {{c2::His angels}}, {{c3::His books}}, {{c4::His messengers}}, {{c5::the Last Day}}, and {{c6::<bdi>القَدَر</bdi> (qadar)}}

{{c1::Tawḥīd}} is the cornerstone of ʿaqīdah. Its three components: Allah is without partner in His {{c2::dominion}}; without likeness in His {{c3::essence (<bdi>ذَات</bdi>) and attributes (<bdi>صِفَات</bdi>)}}; and alone {{c4::deserving of worship}}

cards.front: What does belief in the angels comprise?
cards.back: Belief in their existence, their tasks and their descriptions — though we cannot see them

cards.front: Besides the books themselves, what does belief in the books of Allah include?
cards.back: That the last and final book is the Qurʾān

cards.front: What does belief in the messengers require?
cards.back: Accepting every messenger and prophet Allah sent to guide humanity, including the final messenger Muḥammad ﷺ

cards.text: Belief in the Last Day: that there is {{c1::life after death}}, with {{c2::accountability before Allah}}; that it {{c3::lasts for eternity}}; and that {{c4::we will be resurrected}}

cards.front: Which of the six pillars of faith is the most complex and difficult to understand?
cards.back: Belief in <bdi>القَدَر</bdi> (qadar) — divine decree

cards.front: Belief in <bdi>القَدَر</bdi> covers which kinds of decree?
cards.back: Both the good and the bad

cards.text: Belief in <bdi>القَدَر</bdi> includes belief in Allah's {{c1::pre-eternal knowledge}} and in {{c2::<bdi>اللَّوْح المَحْفُوظ</bdi> (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ)}}

cards.front: What is belief in <bdi>القَضَاء</bdi> (al-qaḍāʾ)?
cards.back: Understanding that nothing happens without the will and decree of Allah

cards.front: What must belief in qadar be balanced against?
cards.back: That we still have a level of free will, and are accountable for our own choices

cards.front: What analogy shows Allah's foreknowledge without removing a person's responsibility?
cards.back: A teacher knows which students are putting in effort, so knows who will fail the final — yet the student can blame no one but themselves

cards.text: <bdi>أَمِنَ يَأْمَنُ</bdi> means {{c1::to feel safe}}; its Form IV <bdi>آمَنَ</bdi> means {{c2::to make someone feel safe}}, and later came to convey {{c3::<bdi>تَصْدِيق</bdi> (taṣdīq) — affirming, believing}}

cards.front: Why do scholars' technical definitions of īmān differ?
cards.back: Each defined it within their own theological context

cards.front: Which two schools did the scholars of Kalām mostly belong to?
cards.back: The Ashʿarīs and the Māturīdīs

cards.front: What were the scholars of Kalām often doing, and in whose language?
cards.back: Refuting philosophy — using the language of Greek logic

cards.front: How did the scholars of Kalām define īmān?
cards.back: Affirming everything necessarily known to have come from the religion of the Prophet ﷺ

cards.text: {{c1::التَّصْدِيقُ}} بِمَا عُلِمَ مَجِيئُهُ {{c2::ضَرُورَةً}} مِنْ دِينِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ

cards.front: On the Kalām definition, what kind of act is īmān?
cards.back: An action of the heart alone

cards.front: On the Kalām definition of īmān, what is kufr?
cards.back: Its opposite — not affirming what is necessarily known to be from the Prophet's ﷺ religion

cards.text: The Atharīs defined īmān as belief {{c1::in the heart}}, declaration {{c2::with the tongue}}, and action {{c3::with the limbs}}

cards.front: Which group was the Atharī definition of īmān a response to?
cards.back: The Murjiʾah — <bdi>المُرْجِئَة</bdi>

cards.front: What did the Murjiʾah hold about īmān?
cards.back: That only the actions of the heart are required

cards.front: Complete the Prophet's ﷺ answer about iḥsān: “To worship Allah as if …”
cards.back: …you see Him; and if you do not see Him, He truly sees you

cards.front: What does <bdi>إِحْسَان</bdi> mean linguistically?
cards.back: Perfection, goodness

cards.front: What is iḥsān, technically?
cards.back: Doing things in the best way possible

cards.front: What is iḥsān said to be the hallmark of?
cards.back: An upright, moral, God-conscious believer

cards.front: Of islām, īmān and iḥsān, which is the highest stage?
cards.back: Iḥsān

cards.text: The scholars of Taṣawwuf see two stages of iḥsān in Ḥadīth Jibrīl: {{c1::worshipping as if you see Allah}} — reached only in the hereafter — and {{c2::knowing that He sees you}}, the stage through which iḥsān is achieved now
cards.extra: The second stage is reconstructed from the ḥadīth. Your notes name only the first.

cards.front: In Ḥadīth Jibrīl, what did the Prophet ﷺ reply when asked when the Hour will come?
cards.back: That he knew no more about it than the one asking

cards.front: Whose knowledge alone is the timing of the Hour?
cards.back: Allah's alone

cards.front: Complete the sign of the Hour in Ḥadīth Jibrīl: “The slave woman will give birth to …”
cards.back: …her own owner

cards.front: Complete the sign of the Hour in Ḥadīth Jibrīl: “The barefoot, destitute, unclothed shepherds …”
cards.back: …will compete in building tall buildings

cards.text: “The slave woman will give birth to her owner” is read as {{c1::widespread ignorance of Islamic law}}, or figuratively as {{c2::children treating their mothers like slaves}}
“The shepherds will compete in building tall buildings” is read literally — {{c1::something we see today}} — or figuratively, as {{c2::the affairs of the world turned upside down}}

cards.front: Who narrates the ḥadīth of creation in the womb (Arbaʿīn 4)?
cards.back: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd RA — one of the best-known Companions

cards.front: What is the kunya of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd RA?
cards.back: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān — <bdi>أَبُو عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ</bdi>

cards.front: How early did ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd RA accept Islam?
cards.back: Among the very first to accept it

cards.text: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd RA served the Prophet ﷺ as {{c1::his personal attendant}}: he would {{c2::carry his shoes}}, {{c3::cover him while he bathed}}, and {{c4::wake him when he slept}}

cards.front: For what was ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd RA among the best of the Companions?
cards.back: Reciting the Qurʾān

cards.text: The Companions learned the Qurʾān {{c1::ten verses}} at a time, and did not move on until {{c2::they had understood them and put them into practice}}

cards.front: When the Prophet ﷺ asked ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd RA to recite to him, which sūrah did he recite?
cards.back: Sūrat al-Nisāʾ

cards.front: At which verse did the Prophet ﷺ stop ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd RA's recitation of al-Nisāʾ?
cards.back:
فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جِئْنَا مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ وَجِئْنَا بِكَ عَلَى هَٰؤُلَاءِ شَهِيدًا
“So how will it be when We bring from every community a witness, and bring you, O Muḥammad, as a witness against these?” — al-Nisāʾ 4:41

cards.front: When ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd RA reached al-Nisāʾ 4:41 — “how will it be when We bring from every community a witness…” — how did the Prophet ﷺ respond?
cards.back: His eyes overflowed with tears, and he said, “That is enough now”

cards.front: Whose manners did ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd RA closely resemble?
cards.back: The Prophet's ﷺ

cards.text: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd RA made {{c1::both hijrahs — to Abyssinia and to Madinah}}, and fought in {{c2::every battle}}

cards.front: What part did ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd RA play in the death of Abū Jahl at Badr?
cards.back: He finished him off — two young men of the Anṣār had already struck Abū Jahl down, and Ibn Masʿūd found him dying

cards.front: Where did ʿUmar RA send ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd RA, and to do what?
cards.back: To Kufa, to teach

cards.front: Roughly how many ḥadīth did ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd RA narrate?
cards.back: About 840 — the figure usually given is 848

cards.front: To which Companion do the Ḥanafīs trace their madhhab?
cards.back: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd RA

cards.front: How does ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd RA describe the Prophet ﷺ as he opens the ḥadīth of creation in the womb?
cards.back: “The truthful, the one believed” — <bdi>الصَّادِقُ المَصْدُوقُ</bdi>
cards.source: Arbaʿīn Ḥadīth 4 — the text in translation

cards.text: In the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, each person's creation is gathered in the womb as {{c1::a <bdi>نُطْفَة</bdi> (nuṭfah)}} for forty days, then becomes {{c2::an <bdi>عَلَقَة</bdi> (ʿalaqah)}} for the same, then {{c3::a <bdi>مُضْغَة</bdi> (muḍghah)}} for the same
cards.source: Arbaʿīn Ḥadīth 4 — the text in translation

cards.front: In the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, after how many days is the soul breathed into the fetus?
cards.back: 120 — three stages of forty days each
cards.source: Arbaʿīn Ḥadīth 4 — the text in translation

cards.front: In the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, who breathes the soul into the fetus?
cards.back: The angel sent to it
cards.source: Arbaʿīn Ḥadīth 4 — the text in translation

cards.text: In the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, the angel is commanded to write four things: {{c1::sustenance — <bdi>رِزْق</bdi>}}, {{c2::lifespan — <bdi>أَجَل</bdi>}}, {{c3::deeds — <bdi>عَمَل</bdi>}}, and {{c4::whether wretched or happy — <bdi>شَقِيّ أَمْ سَعِيد</bdi>}}
cards.extra: In the order of the ḥadīth.
cards.source: Arbaʿīn Ḥadīth 4 — the text in translation

cards.front: In the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, what does the Prophet ﷺ say just before describing how people's lives end?
cards.back: He swears an oath: “By Allah, besides whom there is no god”
cards.source: Arbaʿīn Ḥadīth 4 — the text in translation

cards.text: In the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, one of you does the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only {{c1::a forearm's length — <bdi>ذِرَاع</bdi>}} between him and it; then {{c2::what has been written overtakes him}}, and {{c3::he does the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it}}
cards.source: Arbaʿīn Ḥadīth 4 — the text in translation

cards.front: In the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, what is the reverse of the one who does the deeds of the people of Paradise and ends in the Fire?
cards.back: One who does the deeds of the people of the Fire until only a forearm's length remains; then what is written overtakes him, and he does the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it
cards.source: Arbaʿīn Ḥadīth 4 — the text in translation

cards.front: Which collections relate the ḥadīth of creation in the womb?
cards.back: Both al-Bukhārī and Muslim — it is <bdi>مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِ</bdi> (muttafaq ʿalayh)
cards.source: Arbaʿīn Ḥadīth 4 — the text in translation

cards.front: The ḥadīth of creation in the womb describes the fetus's stages. What is that description counted as evidence of?
cards.back: The Prophet's ﷺ prophethood — it is one of the proofs of prophethood, which are a whole field of study

cards.front: In the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, what is the <bdi>نُطْفَة</bdi> (nuṭfah)?
cards.back: The mixture of male and female fluid in the womb — usually translated “drop”

cards.front: In modern terms, what do some take the <bdi>نُطْفَة</bdi> stage of the ḥadīth of creation in the womb to be?
cards.back: The zygote — the sperm and the egg combined

cards.front: What does <bdi>عَلَقَة</bdi> (ʿalaqah), the second stage in the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, mean?
cards.back: A suspended or clinging thing; a clot

cards.front: What happens to the embryo during the <bdi>عَلَقَة</bdi> stage of the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, in modern terms?
cards.back: The fertilized egg implants in the wall of the uterus and clings to it

cards.front: What does <bdi>مُضْغَة</bdi> (muḍghah), the third stage in the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, mean?
cards.back: A chewed lump; a lump of flesh — what the embryo looks like at that stage

cards.front: Besides the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, where are the stages <bdi>نُطْفَة</bdi>, <bdi>عَلَقَة</bdi> and <bdi>مُضْغَة</bdi> described?
cards.back: In the Qurʾān — e.g. al-Muʾminūn 23:13–14

cards.front: Why is the breathing-in of the soul, in the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, taken as the moment the fetus is given life?
cards.back: Because the soul — <bdi>الرُّوح</bdi> — is what gives a human being life

cards.text: Two definitions of the soul, <bdi>الرُّوح</bdi>: al-Nawawī — {{c1::a delicate substance interwoven with the human body}}; al-Ghazālī — {{c2::an independent substance that traverses the body}}

cards.front: How much knowledge of the soul, <bdi>الرُّوح</bdi>, have we been given?
cards.back: Very little — <bdi>وَمَا أُوتِيتُمْ مِنَ العِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا</bdi> (al-Isrāʾ 17:85)

cards.front: In the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, what does the <bdi>رِزْق</bdi> written for each person cover?
cards.back: Everything they will receive: wealth, food, water, shelter, clothing and provisions

cards.front: What follows from a person's <bdi>رِزْق</bdi> being written before birth?
cards.back: They will receive neither more nor less than what was decided

cards.front: What follows from a person's <bdi>أَجَل</bdi>, their lifespan, being written before birth?
cards.back: They will not leave this world a moment earlier or later than decided

cards.front: In the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, which of a person's deeds are written?
cards.back: All of them — good or bad, big or small, public or private

cards.front: In the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, what does “wretched or happy” — <bdi>شَقِيّ أَمْ سَعِيد</bdi> — refer to?
cards.back: Where the person will end up in the hereafter: their salvation, or not

cards.front: What should the endings described in the ḥadīth of creation in the womb make us feel about our own?
cards.back: Uneasy — never complacent because we are doing well now; no one knows how they will leave

cards.front: In light of the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, what should we ask of Allah about our end?
cards.back: His help to a good ending — <bdi>حُسْن الخَاتِمَة</bdi> — and His protection from a bad one — <bdi>سُوء الخَاتِمَة</bdi>

cards.front: What lesson about resurrection is drawn from the ḥadīth of creation in the womb?
cards.back: Certainty in it: the One who makes us through so complex a process, a sign of His might, can also bring us back from the dead

cards.front: What lesson about doing important things is drawn from the ḥadīth of creation in the womb?
cards.back: Be careful and deliberate, and take your time — there is no need to rush or be hasty

cards.front: Based on the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, when do the majority of scholars hold that life begins?
cards.back: 120 days after conception — the basis for understanding the ruling on abortion

cards.front: How does Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam's fatwa on abortion define abortion?
cards.back: Expelling the fetus from the womb, by drugs or by suction

cards.front: What principle does Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam's fatwa on abortion put first and foremost?
cards.back: Islam regards human life as sacred, wherever that life exists

cards.front: What status does the Sharīʿah give a human body after death?
cards.back: As sacred as it was before death

cards.front: Into which two stages does Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam's fatwa on abortion divide its ruling?
cards.back: Before the soul enters the fetus (the first 120 days), and after

cards.front: Per Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam's fatwa on abortion, what is the ruling on abortion after the soul has entered the fetus (after 120 days)?
cards.back: Totally unlawful and tantamount to murder — the scholars have unanimously condemned it

cards.front: Per Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam's fatwa on abortion, when have some scholars given a <bdi>رُخْصَة</bdi> to abort after the soul has entered?
cards.back: When the mother's life is in certain and absolute danger

cards.front: On what juristic principle does the <bdi>رُخْصَة</bdi> to abort, when the mother's life is in certain danger, rest?
cards.back: Faced with two evils, choose the lesser — a principle of uṣūl al-fiqh and the qawāʿid

cards.front: When the mother's life conflicts with her unborn child's, why is hers saved?
cards.back: She is established in life, with duties and responsibilities; the child is still in the womb

cards.front: Per Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam's fatwa on abortion, why is abortion unlawful even before the soul enters the fetus?
cards.back: The fetus is part of the mother's body — like her own life and organs, a trust from the Creator that she has no right to abort

cards.front: Abortion before the soul enters the fetus is not murder. What sin is it?
cards.back: Violating the rights of one's own organs

cards.text: Circumstances that can allow abortion before the soul enters the fetus: {{c1::conception through rape}}; {{c2::danger to the mother's life or health}}; {{c3::repeated pregnancies severely damaging her health}}
cards.extra: Not a closed list. From Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam's fatwa on abortion.

cards.front: Per Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam's fatwa on abortion, which pregnancy is not a reason for abortion, though rape can be?
cards.back: Pregnancy from unlawful intimacy

cards.front: What has been recorded in <bdi>اللَّوْح المَحْفُوظ</bdi>, the Preserved Tablet?
cards.back: Everything that has happened, is happening and will happen — good or bad from our perspective

cards.text: Nothing happens without the will and decree of Allah — even {{c1::all human actions, good and bad, and the intentions and thoughts behind them}} are brought into existence by Him

cards.front: What is the human share of choice — the choice to do something or not — called?
cards.back: <bdi>كَسْب</bdi> (kasb) — acquisition

cards.front: What follows from human beings having <bdi>كَسْب</bdi> (kasb)?
cards.back: They are legally responsible, and deserve reward or punishment

cards.text: The position of Ahl al-Sunnah wa-l-Jamāʿah on human choice lies between {{c1::coercion}} and {{c2::absolute free will}} — we can choose between the choices before us

cards.front: Why should one not delve too deeply into qadar?
cards.back: It is beyond our understanding — it confused even the Companions

cards.front: What does science not fully understand that parallels the limits of understanding qadar?
cards.back: How thoughts form, turn into intentions, and turn into actions

cards.front: Which saying of the Prophet ﷺ makes a person's ending decisive for their deeds?
cards.back: “Actions are judged by their endings” — <bdi>إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالخَوَاتِيمِ</bdi> (al-Bukhārī)
